summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked; one WebSearch used). All empirical items are PENDING; no values were taken from search snippets. The r1 search confirmed that OAG annual reports (61st and 63rd identified), NPC reviews of the national-pride list and 2026 press coverage of repeated extensions exist; these are recorded as leads pointing to primary OAG/NPC records. Main output is the estimation design for DeliveryConstraints: a project-level panel from five sample frames (OAG/MoF national-pride panel, NPC project bank, World Bank and ADB completed projects, PPMO/OCDS contracts, plus a reconstruction reference class), harmonised for BS/AD/Nepal-FY dates, constant prices and FX, stratified by sector, financier, size and terrain. Approval lag and time overrun are estimated as right-censored duration distributions (Kaplan-Meier plus log-normal accelerated failure time), cost overrun as a log-normal distribution of real (1+overrun) ratios on the decision-to-build baseline, construction capacity as the P90 of sustained annual output, and execution rate as the ratio of planned to actual duration (cross-checked with 02B financial execution). Q2 (maintenance gap) is designed as DoR/Roads Board requirement minus Red Book/Road Maintenance Fund funding. Q3 (PPP) is an inventory of legal frameworks and a survival analysis of IBN/PPI projects from PDA to financial close and operation. Reported 2026 flood damage to Trishuli-basin infrastructure is recorded as an unverified event without numbers. 41 source leads (29 reused from the shared register, 8 general-knowledge URLs flagged unverified, 4 secondary press pointers from the r1 search).

findings.claim: Q1: Time overrun on national pride projects: original vs latest approved completion date and number of extensions per project.
findings.note: OAG 61st-63rd annual reports and MoF Economic Survey pride-project annex; BS dates converted to AD and Nepal FY with documented rule. Leads: 06C-L01, 06C-L02, 06C-L06, 06C-L23, 06C-L35, 06C-L36, 06C-L38

findings.claim: Q1: Cost overrun on national pride projects: latest revised cost estimate vs original approved cost, nominal and deflated.
findings.note: Report nominal ratio and real ratio (deflated with NSO construction/GFCF deflator); separate scope change from price escalation where OAG/NPC records allow. Leads: 06C-L01, 06C-L06, 06C-L37, 06C-L38

findings.claim: Q1: Time and cost overruns on completed donor-financed infrastructure projects (ADB PCRs/PVRs, World Bank ICRs/ICR Reviews): original vs actual closing, appraisal vs actual cost.
findings.note: Donor records are better documented but selected; report separately from GoN-financed projects. Leads: 06C-L12, 06C-L13, 06C-L14, 06C-L15, 06C-L16, 06C-L17
findings.period: projects closed 2000-2026 (calendar dates; convert to Nepal FY)

findings.claim: Q1: Approval lag (approval to construction start) distribution by sector and financier.
findings.note: Approval lag = time from formal approval (NPC project bank entry / cabinet decision / donor Board approval) to construction start (first civil-works contract award or notice to proceed). Time overrun ratio = actual (or current forecast) duration / originally approved duration, measured from construction start. Leads: 06C-L07, 06C-L12, 06C-L13, 06C-L15, 06C-L25

findings.claim: Q1: Contract-level variation orders and time extensions on civil-works contracts (PPMO/OCDS).
findings.note: Contract amendment value / original contract value; extensions in days. Leads: 06C-L24, 06C-L25, 06C-L26

findings.claim: Q2: Road maintenance requirement (routine, recurrent, periodic) vs funded maintenance allocation, SRN, by Nepal FY.
findings.note: Requirement from DoR Annual Road Maintenance Plan (RMMS/HDM); funding from Roads Board and Red Book maintenance heads; gap = requirement - funding. Leads: 06C-L18, 06C-L19, 06C-L20, 06C-L21, 06C-L22

findings.claim: Q2: Maintenance funding gap for irrigation, water supply and public buildings.
findings.note: Red Book heads; requirement norms from sector ministries (no lead yet for requirement). Leads: 06C-L20, 06C-L21, 06C-L22

findings.claim: Q3: PPP legal framework inventory (BOOT Act 2006, PPP Policy, PPP and Investment Act 2019 and amendments) and institutional roles.
findings.note: Legal texts only; dates from gazette. Leads: 06C-L28, 06C-L31, 06C-L30

findings.claim: Q3: PPP track record: projects reaching PDA/financial close/operation vs projects stalled or cancelled, by sector (IBN and line ministries; PPI database).
findings.note: Kaplan-Meier survival from PDA/approval to financial close and to COD, consistent with 05A licence-cohort method; hydropower IPPs under electricity licensing kept separate (05A). Leads: 06C-L29, 06C-L33, 06C-L30, 06C-L32

findings.claim: Contractor/construction capacity: sustained maximum annual physical output (e.g. SRN blacktopping, bridges completed) and concurrent contracts per contractor class.
findings.note: max_units_per_year = high quantile (P90) of annual delivered units over a 10-year window, by asset type; concurrency from OCDS. Leads: 06C-L19, 06C-L23, 06C-L25, 06C-L26

findings.claim: Reported 2026 flood damage to Trishuli-basin infrastructure (hydropower plants and headworks, Pasang Lhamu/Rasuwagadhi road, bridges, Rasuwagadhi border facilities): UNVERIFIED event. Extent, assets affected, repair cost and outage duration to be confirmed from BIPAD/NDRRMA, DoR, NEA/IPPAN, DoED and any government damage assessment.
findings.note: No numbers recorded. Once verified, it serves (a) as a capital-stock shock observation for 13A/X18 (damage values only) and (b) as a test of reconstruction lag (entered in the lag panel as a separate 'reconstruction' reference class). Leads: 06C-L39, 06C-L40

findings.claim: 06C-A1: For ongoing projects, time overrun is right-censored at the latest report date; distributions are estimated with survival methods rather than by dropping incomplete projects.
06C-A2: Cost overrun baseline is the cost approved at decision to build (first NPC/cabinet approval or donor appraisal), not a later revised estimate.
06C-A3: Until r2 estimates exist, any use of DeliveryConstraints in scenarios must declare parameters as labelled assumptions in config/model_config.yaml (owned by the orchestrator), not as evidence.

assumptions.text: Pre-r2 DeliveryConstraints parameters are labelled assumptions only.

challenges.text: Financial capex execution (spent / budget) is not the same as physical execution. DeliveryConstraints.execution_rate should be estimated from physical progress vs plan (06C) and cross-checked with 02B's financial series; please keep the two separate in the model register.

Hydropower completion rates: 06C will reuse the 05A licence-cohort Kaplan-Meier method for PPP/IBN projects; please confirm the censoring date and failure definition so the two are comparable, and avoid counting IBN hydropower projects in both.
OAG extraction: 06C needs project-level tables (cost, dates, progress) from the same OAG reports 11B and 02B use; propose one shared extraction keyed by OAG report number, chapter and table.

The reported 2026 Trishuli-basin flood should enter the capital-stock shock channel only as PDNA-style damage (asset) values once verified; 06C records the reconstruction duration separately as a lag reference class, not as damage.

DeliveryConstraints.approval_lag_years is an integer and execution_rate a point value; scenario runs should pass quantiles (median, P75, P90) of the 06C distributions as separate stress settings rather than a single mean.

uncertainty: No values in r1. Expected uncertainty is large and asymmetric: overrun distributions for infrastructure are right-skewed, OAG samples over-represent troubled projects, donor records under-represent GoN-only projects, and ongoing projects are censored. Cost overruns mix scope change, price escalation and FX effects which must be separated. Maintenance requirement estimates depend on DoR model assumptions. The 2026 Trishuli-basin damage is unverified.

estimation_design.unit_of_observation: project (and, where available, civil-works contract) with sector, financier, province, approval date, construction start, original completion date, latest/actual completion date, original cost, latest/actual cost, currency, price basis, status (completed/ongoing/cancelled/terminated)

sample_frames.source: OAG annual reports panel (52nd-63rd), MoF Economic Survey annexes, NPC reviews
sample_frames.bias: OAG focuses on problem projects -> upward bias; use all listed pride projects, not only those discussed

sample_frames.use: approval dates and approved costs for broader, less selected sample

sample_frames.frame: World Bank closed investment projects in Nepal
sample_frames.use: board approval -> effectiveness -> closing (original vs actual); cost at appraisal vs actual from ICR annexes
PCR/PVR appraisal vs actual cost and closing dates; reasons for delay
contract-level extensions and variations; contractor concurrency

sample_frames.frame: Reconstruction reference class (2015 earthquake; 2026 Trishuli event if verified)

harmonisation: BS dates -> AD -> Nepal FY with documented conversion (FY starts mid-July)
costs to constant prices with NSO construction/GFCF deflator; FX-denominated costs kept in USD and converted at NRB rates with FX effect reported separately
project restructurings: keep original baseline; record each revision as a separate observation
donor 'closing date' is a financing date, not physical completion: flag and, where ICR states physical completion, use that
stratification: sector (roads/bridges, hydropower, irrigation, water supply, airports, urban, buildings)

delivery_lag_distribution.definitions: Approval lag = time from formal approval (NPC project bank entry / cabinet decision / donor Board approval) to construction start (first civil-works contract award or notice to proceed). Time overrun ratio = actual (or current forecast) duration / originally approved duration, measured from construction start.
delivery_lag_distribution.method: Kaplan-Meier for approval->start and start->completion with censoring at latest report date; log-normal AFT with covariates (sector, financier, size, terrain, post-2017); report median, P75, P90 by stratum. approval_lag_years = ceil(median) for central case; P75/P90 for stress cases. execution_rate = planned duration / actual (or forecast) duration, bounded to [0,1], by stratum; cross-check with 02B physical/financial execution.

capacity_parameter.method: P90 of annual physical output over FY2015/16-FY2025/26 by asset type; contractor concurrency from OCDS

cost_overrun_distribution.maps_to: unit_cost (uplift applied to engineering unit-cost estimates)
cost_overrun_distribution.definition: overrun = latest or actual cost / cost at decision to build - 1; nominal and real (constant prices); FX effect separate
cost_overrun_distribution.method: fit log-normal to (1+real overrun) by stratum; report median, mean, P80, P90; reference-class uplift = quantile at chosen acceptable-overrun risk; compare GoN vs donor vs PPP; contract-level variation-order distribution as lower bound

legal_framework: PPP and Investment Act 2019 and amendments
ppp_track_record.method: inventory of IBN/line-ministry PPP and large private projects; Kaplan-Meier from approval/PDA to financial close and COD; outcomes: operational, under construction, stalled, cancelled; benchmark with PPI database and BI 2023 scores

maintenance_gap.method: requirement (DoR ARMP, by category) minus funded allocation (Roads Board RMF + Red Book maintenance heads), Nepal FY, NPR current and constant

unverified_events.event: Reported 2026 flood damage to Trishuli-basin infrastructure
